sources.name: EGNOS Message Server (EMS) User Interface Document
sources.reference: E-RD-SYS-E31-011-ESA, Issue 2 Revision 0, 2004-11-26, section 3, page 14, figures 3 and 4
supports: a data record holds PRN, a two-digit year, month, day, hour, minute and second, the message type, and the message in hexadecimal
blank characters separate the data fields and a line feed ends each record
the time stamp is GPS time from Issue 2 Revision 0 onward; earlier EMS issues used UTC
the message type is derived from message bits 9 to 14

sources.name: gLAB EGNOS v2.0 file description page
supports: three consecutive whitespace-separated records for PRN 120 spanning 2018-03-31 23:59:58 through 2018-04-01 00:00:00
each record carries a 64-character hexadecimal message, that is the 32-byte framed form

expectations: The GPS week and seconds of week pinned by the test were computed from the printed calendar fields with the Sunday-origin 1980-01-06 GPS week epoch, independently of the parser under test: 1994/604798, 1994/604799 and 1995/0.
The expected bytes pinned by the test were converted from the hexadecimal text displayed on the source page, not read back from a parse result.
limits: One authored example of the Issue 2 layout. It does not stand in for a real archive file, for a multi-band EMS product, or for the pre-Issue 2 UTC time stamps.
All three records carry the same PRN and the same message type, so neither field is varied by this fixture.
